meta.title: ShramkoGSFPV — FPV drone simulator for real 3D scans, in your browser
meta.description: Free, open-source FPV simulator that flies real Gaussian Splatting scans from SuperSplat: Betaflight-style rates and PID, walls you crash into, your radio over USB or touch sticks. No install.

hero.h1: Fly an FPV drone through real 3D scans — right in your browser
hero.sub: ShramkoGSFPV turns SuperSplat Gaussian Splatting scans into places you can fly: Betaflight-style rates and PID, walls you actually crash into, and your own radio over USB or touch sticks. Nothing to install.
hero.ctaNote: Works best in desktop Chrome or Edge with WebGPU.

paste.label: Or paste a SuperSplat link

paste.empty: Paste a SuperSplat link or a scene id first.

how.h2: Three steps from a scan to the air
how.lead: No account, no download. The scene streams straight from SuperSplat into your browser.

steps.d: Start with one of Andrii's scans or paste the link to any public SuperSplat scene.
Plug in an EdgeTX radio in USB joystick mode (WebHID), use a gamepad, or fly with touch sticks.
Move the sticks once to calibrate, arm with the throttle all the way down — like a real quad — and go.

real.h2: A quad that behaves like the one in your hands
real.lead: An own flight model — four motors, a mixer and a rate PID — flying inside the real geometry of the scan.

items.d: Every physics tick sweeps the drone's body against the scan's voxel collision data, so a fast quad can't slip through a thin wall between frames.
Hit something hard and the quad tumbles and throws debris. Brush a wall gently and it slides along it.
Betaflight, Actual, KISS and Raceflight rate curves match Betaflight 4.5.1's own code with 0 error at 1880 points, both computed in double precision (in float32 they differ by at most 0.00063 °/s).
Flights are recorded as stick input and replay deterministically: the same inputs always give the same flight.
Earth, Moon, Mars or zero-g. On the Moon the same drone gets extremely twitchy — the “keep thrust-to-weight” switch tames it.

risks.lead: Short and honest, so nothing catches you by surprise.

items.t: Scene data can change without notice
items.d: Scenes load from SuperSplat's public but undocumented CDN. It can change at any time, and some scenes may stop loading.

items.t: Some scans come without collision data
items.d: For those, the simulator can build walls right in your browser with SuperSplat’s own tool (up to 4 million Gaussians, about 25 seconds for a 2.1-million scan on a desktop GPU). Bigger scans stay fly-through.

Crashes and fast flight can make you queasy, so take breaks. Measured over 50 crashes, effects flash at most 2 times per second, under the WCAG limit of 3; your reduced-motion setting is respected (not tested yet).

items.t: A simulator is not a real flight
items.d: Practise responsibly, follow your local drone law and never fly over people.
Calibration, flight history and favourites are stored only in your browser.

items.q: How can I fly an FPV drone through a 3D Gaussian Splatting scan?
items.a: Open ShramkoGSFPV in desktop Chrome or Edge, pick one of Andrii's scans or paste a SuperSplat link, connect a radio, a gamepad or touch sticks, then calibrate, arm and fly. There is nothing to install.

items.q: Can I use my RadioMaster radio in the browser?
items.a: That is what it is built for: switch an EdgeTX radio such as the TX16S, Boxer, Pocket or Zorro to USB joystick mode and connect it over WebHID in Chrome or Edge. So far this has been tested only in Chrome with a simulated EdgeTX radio, not with real hardware or in Edge.

items.q: Is there a free FPV simulator that runs in the browser?
items.a: Yes. ShramkoGSFPV is free and open source under the MIT license. It runs on WebGPU in desktop Chrome or Edge, with no download.

items.q: Which SuperSplat scenes can I fly?
items.a: Any public SuperSplat scene, by link or id. Scenes published with voxel collision data have solid walls at once; for the others you can build walls in your browser with one click (scans up to 4 million Gaussians). Bigger scans can be flown through but not crashed into.

items.q: Does it work on iPad or phone?
items.a: Touch sticks have been tested only in desktop Chrome's touch emulation, not in Safari, on iPad or in Android browsers yet, and you need a browser with WebGPU. Radios need desktop Chrome or Edge.

items.q: Is the flight physics like Betaflight?
items.a: The rate curves (Betaflight, Actual, KISS, Raceflight) match Betaflight 4.5.1's own code with 0 error at 1880 points when both are computed in double precision, and a rate PID drives four motors through a mixer. It is our own flight model, not Betaflight firmware.

items.q: Do I crash into walls or fly through them?
items.a: On scenes with collision data you crash: the drone's body is swept against the voxel data on every physics tick, and a test harness checks that fast flight cannot tunnel through walls. See Live numbers for the result.
Yes, MIT. Code, measurements and design decisions are on GitHub. Betaflight's formulas were re-implemented; no GPL code was copied.

opensource.h2: MIT-licensed and built in the open
opensource.lead: Code, measurements and every design decision live on GitHub. Pull requests, test reports from real radios and new scans are welcome.

privacy.title: Privacy — ShramkoGSFPV
privacy.description: What ShramkoGSFPV collects, why, for how long, and your rights under the GDPR.

p: The controller of your data is Andrii Shramko. You can reach him at zmei116@gmail.com or through the contact form on this site.

The site sends a few whitelisted events to its own server at /api/e: switching language, clicks on the main buttons and contact links, and opening a scene. No cookies are set, no device identifier is created and your IP address is not stored.
Purpose: understanding which parts of the site are useful (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Events are kept for 12 months.

sections.h: Google Analytics — only with your consent
p: If analytics is switched on for this site, a banner asks first. Google's script is not loaded until you press Accept. Consent mode starts with every storage type denied, and Accept grants analytics storage only.
Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). You can withdraw it at any time.
Radio calibration, flight history and favourites stay in your browser's storage. They are strictly necessary for the simulator to work, never leave your device and need no consent.
If you send the form, your email, the role you chose and your message are stored on the server and forwarded to the owner's Telegram notification bot.
They are kept until your request is handled or until you ask for them to be deleted. Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).

Scene preview images on this page, and the scenes themselves in the simulator, are loaded by your browser directly from PlayCanvas servers (SuperSplat). As with any website, those servers see your IP address.

You can ask for access to your data, its correction or erasure, restriction of processing, data portability, and you can object to processing or withdraw consent — through the contact form or by email.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Polish supervisory authority, the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO).

items.name: Rapier
